# How Often AI Recommends Your Business

URL: https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/
Updated: 2026-11-18

> Local AI Registry reviews 14 sources: ask AI the same thing twice and Gemini’s sources overlap by only 0.46. How to measure how often AI recommends you.

[Home](https://localairegistry.com/index.html) / How often AI recommends you

Research

# How Often AI Recommends Your Business

By [Steve Lee](https://localairegistry.com/team/steve-lee/index.html), founder of Local AI Registry  
Updated November 16, 2026

## Key findings

1. In research reviewed by Local AI Registry, the same query run twice shared 0.78 of its sources on Google Search, 0.66 on Google AI Overviews and 0.46 on Gemini (Grossman et al., SIGIR 2026).
2. In a preprint census of cafés, restaurants and bars in Bali reviewed by Local AI Registry, the overlap between repeated runs of the same query ranged from 0.45 for Gemini to 0.22 for Claude.
3. When ChatGPT was asked the same local question twice, a median of 39 minutes apart, a median of 29% of the businesses named in either answer were named in both, according to 8ight.AI data reviewed by Local AI Registry.
4. Only 10.8% of doctors named by an AI model without web search matched a real clinician in the queried city, versus 63.9% with web search on, in a preprint audit of the 100 largest US metro areas reviewed by Local AI Registry.
5. Wording changes who AI recommends: 74.7% of the people recommended for “an oculoplastic surgeon” were oculoplastic specialists, versus 46.6% for “a doctor who does eyelid lifts,” in a peer-reviewed study reviewed by Local AI Registry.
6. ChatGPT declined to recommend an orthopedic surgeon in 52.8% of 40,500 persona-based requests, and stated income, insurance status and location were the strongest predictors of a recommendation, according to research reviewed by Local AI Registry.
7. Only 3.5% of the businesses ChatGPT named in localized searches appeared at every point tested across a town, according to BrightLocal’s 2026 analysis reviewed by Local AI Registry.
8. In the Bali census reviewed by Local AI Registry, 85.6% of venues were never recommended by any of the four AI systems, and being named was associated with documentation such as a website, more reviews, listed prices and mentions elsewhere on the web.
9. Local AI Registry calculated that a business named in 40% of AI answers has a 95% confidence interval of roughly 17% to 69% after 10 answers and 31% to 50% after 100, so one answer cannot measure AI visibility.

## What is AI visibility, and why can’t one answer measure it?

Visibility in AI-generated local recommendations is best measured as how often a business is named under stated conditions. A single answer is a genuine observation, but on its own it cannot reliably estimate that frequency.

Consumers are adopting generative assistants for local decisions at speed. In BrightLocal’s 2026 survey of 1,002 US consumers, 45% reported using ChatGPT or another generative AI tool to find local businesses, up from 6% a year earlier.[1](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-1) As the behavior has spread, so has an informal method of judging it. An owner, marketer or analyst asks an assistant for the best provider in a category and city, and reads the reply as a verdict on where a business stands.

That reading carries over an assumption from conventional search, where a page of results could reasonably be treated as a ranking. A generative assistant does not return a stored list. It composes an answer at the moment of the request, from whatever it retrieves and infers under that request’s particular conditions. The research reviewed here points to a different unit of analysis.

### Terms used in this brief

AI visibility
:   How often, how prominently and how accurately a business is named in AI answers, measured as a rate across many answers to the same question.

Recommendation frequency
:   The share of AI answers that name a business under a stated set of systems, configurations, locations, phrasings and dates.

Answer engine optimization (AEO)
:   Making a business’s facts clear, consistent and machine-readable so AI systems include it accurately in their answers.

Generative engine optimization (GEO)
:   The academic term for optimizing content to be cited by generative AI search engines; used interchangeably with AEO.

Overlap (Jaccard similarity)
:   What two runs returned in both, divided by what they returned in either. 1 means identical results; 0 means nothing in common.

Confidence interval
:   The range that likely contains the true rate. A 95% interval only becomes narrow after many answers have been collected.

Web search (grounding)
:   When an AI assistant searches the web during a request instead of answering only from what its model learned in training.

Algorithm audit
:   A way to study a system that cannot be inspected directly, by querying it repeatedly and recording what it returns.

Preprint
:   A research paper shared publicly before peer review.

## Does AI recommend the same businesses every time you ask?

No. When the same query was run twice, Gemini’s sources overlapped by only 0.46, and in a census of Bali venues, Claude’s repeated local recommendations overlapped by just 0.22.

Variation in search results is not new. In a 2015 measurement study of Google Search, Kliman-Silver and colleagues found that 18% to 34% of results for local queries changed with the searcher’s location, and that local queries were also the noisiest category when repeated from the same place at the same time.[2](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-2) Generative systems add another layer of variability, because the answer is written rather than retrieved.

The clearest controlled comparison is a study presented at ACM SIGIR 2026 that examined Google Search, Google’s AI Overviews and Gemini on more than 11,000 real user queries.[3](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-3) When the same query was run twice, the overlap between the sources each system drew on, measured by Jaccard similarity, was 0.78 for conventional Search, 0.66 for AI Overviews and 0.46 for Gemini. Minor edits to a query, such as expanding a contraction or adding a question mark, reduced the rank-weighted similarity of AI Overview sources by 29%, compared with 14% for conventional Search.

Audits of local recommendations show the same pattern in the businesses named. A pre-registered census of every café, restaurant and bar in two Bali submarkets, conducted by a company that sells AI-visibility tools, collected 2,208 answers from four assistants over seven days.[4](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-4) Overlap between repeated runs of the same query ranged from 0.22 for Claude to 0.45 for Gemini. The study’s most consequential finding concerns time. When the queries were repeated two weeks later, overlap with the original answers (0.375) was comparable to overlap between reruns within the same period, and the author attributes most of the variation to sampling rather than drift.

**Figure 1. Ask the same question twice and Gemini's sources overlap by only 0.46, versus 0.78 for Google Search.** When the same query was run twice, the sources Google Search drew on overlapped by 0.78, Google AI Overviews by 0.66 and Gemini by 0.46 (Grossman et al., SIGIR 2026). In a separate preprint census of Bali venues, the local businesses named overlapped by 0.45 for Gemini down to 0.22 for Claude (Pitenin, 2026). Compare bars within a panel, not across panels. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/ai-recommendations-change-when-same-query-is-repeated.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/ai-recommendations-change-when-same-query-is-repeated.png) · [Phone SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/ai-recommendations-change-when-same-query-is-repeated-mobile.svg)

Data behind this chart

| Panel | System | Overlap between two runs (returned in both ÷ returned in either) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: sources, general queries | Google Search | 0.78 |
| A: sources, general queries | Google AI Overviews | 0.66 |
| A: sources, general queries | Gemini | 0.46 |
| B: venues recommended, Bali | Gemini | 0.45 |
| B: venues recommended, Bali | Perplexity | 0.40 |
| B: venues recommended, Bali | OpenAI | 0.29 |
| B: venues recommended, Bali | Claude | 0.22 |

Embed this figure

The distinction matters for measurement. If answers drifted steadily, the most recent answer would be an imperfect but current reading. If answers instead scatter around a relatively stable underlying tendency, as this evidence suggests, the tendency is the quantity worth estimating. Each answer is one observation of it, and only an accumulation of observations can show how strong it is.

AEO takeaway

One AI answer is a snapshot, not a ranking.

### What to do

Do not judge your AI visibility from one screenshot. Ask the same customer questions several times, on more than one assistant, and count how often your business is named.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s AI visibility audit shows how a business appears in AI answers today, where answers are wrong, and what competitors are cited for.

## What changes which business AI recommends?

Four conditions: the AI system and its settings, the place, the wording of the request, and time. With web search on, 63.9% of the doctors an AI model named matched a real clinician in the queried city, versus 10.8% with it off.

There is no single frequency. A business can be named often under some conditions and rarely under others. The literature identifies four sets of conditions that change the answer, and a credible measurement has to state which of them it holds fixed.

**Figure 2. Four conditions change which business AI recommends: real local doctors named rose from 10.8% to 63.9% with web search on.** System and configuration, place, wording and time each changed AI recommendations in published research. Each mini-chart comes from a different study and metric, so read each one on its own, not across quadrants. Findings selected and grouped by Local AI Registry. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/four-conditions-that-change-which-business-ai-recommends.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/four-conditions-that-change-which-business-ai-recommends.png) · [Phone SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/four-conditions-that-change-which-business-ai-recommends-mobile.svg)

Data behind this chart

| Condition | Finding | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| System and configuration | Doctors matching a real clinician in the queried city, web search off vs on (same model) | 10.8% vs 63.9% | Ibrahim & Zaki, 2026 (preprint) |
| System and configuration | Sources shared by AI Overviews and Gemini, “near me” queries (overlap) | 0.07 | Grossman et al., 2026 |
| Place | Real doctors named without web search, largest vs smallest third of US metro areas | 16.3% vs 9.5% | Ibrahim & Zaki, 2026 (preprint) |
| Place | Businesses ChatGPT named that appeared at every point tested across a town | 3.5% | BrightLocal, 2026 (industry) |
| Wording and context | Oculoplastic specialists recommended: “an oculoplastic surgeon” vs “a doctor who does eyelid lifts” | 74.7% vs 46.6% | Parikh et al., 2024 |
| Wording and context | ChatGPT responses declining to recommend an orthopedic surgeon | 52.8% | Haupt et al., 2026 |
| Time | Overlap with answers collected two weeks later | 0.375 | Pitenin, 2026 (preprint) |
| Time | Businesses named in either of two ChatGPT answers about 39 minutes apart that appeared in both (median) | 29% | 8ight.AI, 2026 (industry) |

Embed this figure

**System and configuration.** The assistant, the model behind it and whether it searches the web during the request all change the outcome. In an audit of provider recommendations across the 100 largest US metropolitan areas, Ibrahim and Zaki found that only 10.8% of doctors named by a proprietary model without web search matched a real clinician in the queried city; with search enabled, the same model reached 63.9%.[5](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-5) Systems also draw on different evidence. For “near me” queries in the SIGIR study, the overlap between sources used by AI Overviews and Gemini was 0.07.[3](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-3) Disagreement between platforms predates generative AI: Li and Hecht found that Google Maps ratings averaged about 0.7 stars higher than Yelp ratings for the same restaurants, and that the two platforms’ top-ten lists for a metropolitan area overlapped little.[6](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-6)

**Place.** Location operates at more than one scale. Between cities, Ibrahim and Zaki found that without search the share of real doctors named fell from 16.3% in the largest third of metropolitan areas to 9.5% in the smallest, a gradient that largely disappeared once search was enabled.[5](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-5) Haupt and colleagues found ChatGPT more likely to recommend an orthopedic surgeon for prompts set in New York City and Chicago than in Phoenix and Houston.[7](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-7) Within a single town, BrightLocal’s 2026 analysis of localized searches found that only 3.5% of the businesses ChatGPT named appeared at every point tested across the area.[8](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-8) Location effects are not uniform, however. For a stratified sample of general queries, the SIGIR study found that moving AI Overview requests from Newark to Austin reduced source similarity by only 0.01 to 0.02 relative to repeated runs from the same place.[3](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-3) How much place matters appears to depend on the system and the kind of question.

**Wording and context.** The words in a request, and what it reveals about the person asking, change who is named. In a peer-reviewed study of chatbot recommendations for oculoplastic surgeons in the 20 largest US cities, 74.7% of the individuals recommended in response to “an oculoplastic surgeon” were oculoplastic specialists, compared with 46.6% for “a doctor who does eyelid lifts.”[9](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-9) Haupt and colleagues submitted 40,500 persona-based requests for orthopedic surgeons to ChatGPT. It declined to recommend anyone in 52.8% of responses, and stated income, insurance status and location were the strongest predictors of whether a recommendation was given.[7](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-7) Research on brand recommendations points the same way: language models recommended luxury gifts disproportionately to people from high-income countries.[10](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-10)

**Time.** Repetition alone changes answers, as both the SIGIR study and the Bali census show, and it does so over short intervals. 8ight.AI’s 2026 study of local trades found that when ChatGPT was asked the same question twice, a median of 39 minutes apart, a median of 29% of the businesses named in either answer were named in both.[11](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-11) Over longer periods the systems themselves change, as model versions, retrieval sources and defaults are updated, which is why studies such as Parikh’s describe their findings as a record of a single point in time.[9](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-9)

AEO takeaway

State the conditions, or the number means nothing.

### What to do

When you check what AI says about your business, write down the assistant, whether it searched the web, the city, the exact wording and the date, and keep them the same when you check again.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry keeps an owner-confirmed public record of each business, so assistants that search the web find the same verified facts every time they look.

## What can AI visibility research prove, and what can’t it?

It can show how often, and under which conditions, a business is named. It cannot show why. Only 51.5% of sentences written by generative search engines were fully supported by their citations, and 38.3% of ChatGPT’s surgeon suggestions in one study were excluded on review.

Three limits shape what any measurement of AI visibility can claim.

The first is that being named and being named first appear to be different outcomes. In the Bali census, 85.6% of venues were never recommended by any of the four systems. Inclusion was associated with documentation, including having a website, more reviews, listed prices and mentions elsewhere on the web, while star rating was associated only with whether a venue was named first.[4](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-4) These are associations from one hospitality market, reported by a vendor-funded study, but they caution against collapsing inclusion and order into a single rank.

The second is that the sources an assistant displays are imperfect evidence of what produced its answer. In a peer-reviewed audit of four generative search engines, Liu, Zhang and Liang found that only 51.5% of generated sentences were fully supported by their citations, and only 74.5% of citations supported the sentence to which they were attached.[12](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-12) Citation patterns can indicate which sources are prominent in a category. They cannot establish cause.

The third is that a name in an answer is not necessarily a correct name. In the 2023 oculoplastic study, 38.3% of ChatGPT’s suggestions were excluded on review; across the three chatbots studied, the most common reasons were a provider practicing in a different city or not existing at all.[9](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-9) In the orthopedic study, 44.6% of recommended surgeons in a coded subset were valid.[7](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-7) Counting mentions without verifying them can overstate visibility, and in healthcare the cost of that error falls on patients as well as practices.

Underlying all three is a broader point: visibility is partly defined by the instrument that measures it. The foundational paper on generative engine optimization (GEO), the research term for what practitioners call answer engine optimization (AEO), measured visibility with explicitly defined impression metrics and reported that content changes raised it by up to 40% on its benchmark, with effects that varied by domain.[13](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-13) Findings of this kind show that visibility in generative answers responds to content. They do not show that a particular change will produce recommendations, or customers, for a particular business.

AEO takeaway

Being named is not the same as being named correctly.

### What to do

Check that AI answers that name you have the right city, services and details, and fix the sources AI reads when they do not.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry keeps a sourced, dated record of each business, which gives AI a verified source for the business’s name, location and services.

## How should a business measure how often AI recommends it?

Count across many answers under fixed conditions. A business named in 40% of answers has a 95% range of roughly 17% to 69% after 10 answers and 31% to 50% after 100.

If visibility is a frequency to be estimated, its measurement belongs to the tradition of the algorithm audit, which studies a system that cannot be inspected directly by querying it repeatedly and recording what it returns.[14](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/index.html#ref-14) Read together, the evidence above suggests five principles for applying that method to local recommendations.

### Five principles for measuring AI visibility

1. **Report a rate, with its conditions.** The core quantity is the share of answers that name a business under a stated set of systems, configurations, locations, phrasings and dates. A rate reported without its conditions cannot be compared with another.
2. **Collect enough answers to support the claim.** One answer records only whether a business was named on that occasion; it cannot distinguish a business named in nine answers out of ten from one named in one out of ten. Under fixed conditions, a business observed in 40% of answers has a 95% confidence interval of roughly 17% to 69% after ten answers and 31% to 50% after one hundred.
3. **Separate inclusion from order.** Whether a business is named and where it appears when named respond to different factors and should be reported separately.
4. **Verify what is counted.** A mention should count only when the business exists, operates in the location asked about and offers the service requested.
5. **Distinguish noise from change.** A shift between two periods is meaningful only when it exceeds the variation seen within a period under the same protocol, the test the Bali census applied.

**Figure 3. A business named in 40% of AI answers has a 95% range of 17% to 69% after 10 answers and 31% to 50% after 100.** Illustrative calculation by Local AI Registry (95% Wilson score intervals, assuming independent answers under fixed conditions), not study data. The range narrows only as answers accumulate. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/ai-visibility-confidence-interval-by-number-of-answers.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/ai-visibility-confidence-interval-by-number-of-answers.png) · [Phone SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/how-often-ai-recommends-your-business/images/ai-visibility-confidence-interval-by-number-of-answers-mobile.svg)

Data behind this chart

| Answers collected | 95% interval for an observed 40% rate |
| --- | --- |
| 5 | 12% to 77% |
| 10 | 17% to 69% |
| 20 | 22% to 61% |
| 50 | 28% to 54% |
| 100 | 31% to 50% |
| 200 | 33% to 47% |

Embed this figure
AEO takeaway

Measure a rate, not a rank.

### What to do

Track the share of answers that name your business, collect enough answers to trust it, and treat a change as real only when it is bigger than the normal variation between checks.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s free AI Score gives a broader diagnostic of how findable and recommendable a business is to ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity. It is a diagnostic, not the recommendation-frequency measure described in this brief.

## What does this mean for local businesses?

The evidence changes the question worth asking. Whether a given assistant recommends a given business has no stable answer. How often the business is named, by which systems, for which requests, in which places, and how that frequency is moving does. Seen this way, AI visibility is not unknowable. It is measurable in the way other probabilistic systems are measured: through repeated, documented observation, with uncertainty stated and causes claimed only where the evidence supports them.

For local businesses, and for healthcare providers in particular, that discipline separates a reaction to one answer from an understanding of a market position that AI assistants increasingly help to shape. No intervention studied to date guarantees a recommendation. The research does support a narrower and more useful conclusion: visibility in AI-generated local recommendations can be observed, compared and tracked, provided it is estimated from many observations and not inferred from a single answer.

## Who provides AEO services for local businesses?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) is an answer engine optimization company built for local businesses. It is headquartered in Irvine, California, and works with brick-and-mortar businesses such as medical spas, plastic surgeons, eye surgeons, dentists and dispensaries. Its local AEO services include:

* **Free business record.** A public, owner-claimable record of what AI says about the business, with every fact confirmed by the owner.
* **AI visibility audit.** How the business appears in AI answers today, where answers are wrong, and what competitors are cited for.
* **Google Business Profile management.** Location-level hours, holiday hours, services and updates kept current.
* **Press releases and media.** Earned coverage in the news sources AI cites most for local questions.
* **AEO content.** Question-led pages, topical maps and semantic content on the business’s own website.
* **Technical AEO.** LocalBusiness schema, llms.txt, readable pages and AI-readable media.
* **Listing consistency.** Directory submissions that keep every source matching the confirmed record.

Local AI Registry publishes its research openly, including this brief, so business owners can see the evidence behind its methods. Business owners can [look up their business at localairegistry.com/search](https://localairegistry.com/search) and see what AI says about them today.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does ChatGPT recommend the same businesses every time?

No. AI assistants compose a new answer for every request. When ChatGPT was asked the same local question twice, a median of 39 minutes apart, a median of 29% of the businesses named in either answer were named in both, according to 8ight.AI data reviewed by Local AI Registry. In a census of Bali venues, repeated runs of the same query overlapped by 0.22 for Claude and 0.45 for Gemini.

### How do I know if AI recommends my business?

Ask the same customer questions many times, under the same conditions, and count the share of answers that name your business. One answer only shows whether you were named that one time. Local AI Registry’s free business record and AI visibility audit show what ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Perplexity say about a business today.

### How many AI answers do I need to measure my AI visibility?

More than one, and usually many. Local AI Registry calculated that a business named in 40% of answers has a 95% confidence interval of roughly 17% to 69% after 10 answers and 31% to 50% after 100 answers, assuming the conditions stay the same.

### Why does AI recommend different businesses in different places?

Place changes the answer. Without web search, the share of real doctors an AI model named fell from 16.3% in the largest third of US metro areas to 9.5% in the smallest (Ibrahim and Zaki, 2026, preprint). Within one town, BrightLocal found that only 3.5% of the businesses ChatGPT named appeared at every point tested.

### Does web search change which businesses AI recommends?

Yes. In an audit of the 100 largest US metro areas, only 10.8% of doctors named by an AI model without web search matched a real clinician in the queried city; with web search on, the same model reached 63.9% (Ibrahim and Zaki, 2026, preprint).

### Does the wording of a question change who AI recommends?

Yes. In a peer-reviewed study of chatbot recommendations in the 20 largest US cities, 74.7% of the people recommended for “an oculoplastic surgeon” were oculoplastic specialists, compared with 46.6% for “a doctor who does eyelid lifts” (Parikh et al., 2024).

### Can I trust the sources an AI answer cites?

Only partly. In a peer-reviewed audit of four generative search engines, only 51.5% of generated sentences were fully supported by their citations, and only 74.5% of citations supported the sentence they were attached to (Liu, Zhang and Liang, 2023). Citations show which sources are prominent, not what caused the answer.

### Can AEO guarantee that ChatGPT recommends my business?

No. No intervention studied to date guarantees a recommendation. The foundational paper on generative engine optimization found that content changes raised visibility by up to 40% on its benchmark, with effects that varied by domain. That shows visibility responds to content, not that a particular change will bring recommendations or customers to a particular business.

### What is the difference between AEO and GEO?

Generative engine optimization (GEO) and answer engine optimization (AEO) describe the same goal: being cited and described correctly in AI-generated answers. GEO is the term used in academic research; AEO is more common in marketing.

### How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini?

AI assistants name businesses whose facts they can find, read and confirm. Keep your name, location, services and prices clear and identical on your website, Google Business Profile and listings, and judge your visibility across many answers rather than one. Local AI Registry, a free AEO directory for local businesses, gives every business a free, owner-confirmed record at localairegistry.com/search as a starting point.

### What is Local AI Registry?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) is an answer engine optimization (AEO) company and free AEO directory for local businesses, headquartered in Irvine, California. It keeps a verified, owner-confirmed public record of each business so that ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews can find and describe it accurately, and its research team publishes studies on how AI answers local questions.

## Limits of this research

* This brief is an editorial synthesis of published research. Local AI Registry did not collect any of the data cited, and the findings belong to the original authors; Local AI Registry selected, grouped and explained them.
* Preprints have not yet been peer-reviewed and are marked as such. The Bali census was funded and conducted by Norly, an AI-visibility vendor. Industry figures are attributed to the organizations that collected them.
* Each number comes from its own study, population and metric, so values from different studies are not directly comparable.
* Much of the evidence covers healthcare providers in US cities and hospitality venues in Bali. Other business categories and countries may behave differently.
* Figure 3 is an illustrative calculation that assumes independent answers under fixed conditions. It is not study data.
* AI systems change as models, retrieval sources and defaults are updated, so each study is a record of a single point in time.

# The Local Answer Gap: Local AEO Research

URL: https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/
Updated: 2026-11-18

> Local AI Registry’s AEO study of 7,583 Google AI answers: news supplied 67.5% of local citations, business sites 6.5%. Charts, data and an AEO playbook.

[Local AI Registry](https://localairegistry.com)  [Research](https://localairegistry.com/research/index.html)  The Local Answer Gap

Local AI Registry research · Published November 7, 2026

# The Local Answer Gap: what 7,583 Google AI answers reveal about AEO for local businesses

By the [Local AI Registry Research Team](#authors)

The short answer

Local AI Registry’s analysis of 7,583 Google AI Overviews shows that when people ask AI about a local business, the business rarely supplies the answer. In 207 AI answers about local businesses, news outlets supplied two-thirds of the citations and the businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5%. The AI usually answered with chain-wide facts and told people to check with their local store. Answer engine optimization (AEO) closes that gap.

* **55,393** Google searches
* **7,583** AI Overview answers
* **98,020** fact-checked claims
* **1,496** cited pages read
* **29** original charts and explainers

## Key findings

1. Local AI Registry found that local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, the highest of any topic and over five times the 13.7% average (US searches, March to April 2026).
2. In Local AI Registry’s analysis, news outlets supplied 67.5% of citations in Google’s AI answers about local businesses, and Gannett newspapers alone appeared in 90.3% of those answers.
3. Businesses’ own websites supplied only 6.5% of citations in local AI answers, and directories such as Yelp, MapQuest and OpenTable supplied 0.5%, according to Local AI Registry.
4. Local AI Registry found that brand websites ranked on Google’s first page in 147 of 157 brand questions but were cited by Google’s AI in only 70.
5. 83.6% of local AI answers told people to check with their local store, and only 1 of 207 gave a street address or phone number, Local AI Registry found.
6. When Google’s AI attributed a local fact to a store locator, app or official site, 51.6% of those claims were not supported by any page it cited, according to Local AI Registry.
7. Cited social media posts had a median of 8 readable words, and 78% were too thin for AI to verify anything, in Local AI Registry’s review of 1,496 cited pages.
8. Asking the same local question in different words changed about two-thirds of the sources Google’s AI cited, Local AI Registry found.
9. Only 2 of 39,676 queries in public AI search research datasets ask an AI to find a local service provider, according to Local AI Registry’s census.

## What is AEO, and how is it different from SEO?

Search engine optimization (SEO) gets a business into a list of blue links. Answer engine optimization (AEO), also called generative engine optimization (GEO), gets a business into the answer itself: the paragraph that Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity or Microsoft Copilot writes before anyone clicks. To write that paragraph, the AI pieces together facts from sources across the internet. If it can’t find clear, consistent facts about a business, it guesses, hedges or leaves the business out.

Local AI Registry is a local AEO company. It builds a verified public record for each local business, has the owner confirm it, and pushes those facts to the places AI reads. This study asks a simple question: when AI answers a local question today, where do its facts come from, and what should a local business do about it?

**Illustration 1. SEO gets you into the list. AEO gets you into the answer.** Search engine optimization (SEO) earns a place in a list of links. Answer engine optimization (AEO) earns a place inside the AI-written answer that appears before any links. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.png)

Embed this illustration<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.png" alt="Illustration comparing a search results page of blue links (SEO) with an AI answer box that cites a few sources (AEO)" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

Answer engine optimization (AEO)
:   Making a business’s facts clear, consistent and machine-readable so AI systems include it accurately in their answers.

Generative engine optimization (GEO)
:   The academic term for optimizing content to be cited by generative AI search engines; used interchangeably with AEO.

Google AI Overview
:   The AI-written answer Google shows above search results for many queries, with links to the sources it cited.

Citation
:   A source link the AI attaches to its answer. Being cited is how a business’s own pages shape what AI says.

Local intent
:   A search about a physical place: hours, location, services, availability, or finding a provider nearby.

AI visibility
:   How often, how prominently and how accurately a business is named in AI answers, measured as a rate across many answers to the same question.

Google Business Profile
:   Google’s free business listing, which holds a location’s hours, address, services and reviews, and which Google’s AI appears to draw on for store-level facts.

LocalBusiness structured data
:   Schema.org markup on a website that states a business’s name, address, hours and services in a format machines read directly.

## Is anyone studying how AI answers local questions?

Almost no one. Across 39,676 unique queries in four public AI-search research datasets, 239 concern a physical business and only 2 ask an AI to find a local service provider.

**Figure 1. Only 2 of 39,676 public AI-search research queries ask AI to find a local provider.** Across four public AI-search datasets, 239 of 39,676 unique queries (0.6%) concern a physical business, and only 2 ask an AI to find a local service provider. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/public-ai-search-datasets-local-query-census.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/public-ai-search-datasets-local-query-census.png)

Data behind this chart

| Dataset | Unique queries | About a physical business | Ask for a local provider |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IMC 2026 Google AI Overviews | 32,608 | 237 | 0 |
| Organikpi, 13 public datasets | 7,045 | 2 | 2 |
| Cited.io, Oct 2026 | 23 | 0 | 0 |
| Total | 39,676 | 239 | 2 |

Embed this figure<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#public-ai-search-datasets-local-query-census"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/public-ai-search-datasets-local-query-census.png" alt="Table of four public AI search datasets: 39,676 unique queries, 239 about physical businesses, 2 asking for a local provider" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

Every public dataset we found studies informational, software or news queries. The only local questions with real AI answers attached are national chains’ holiday hours, so that is where we looked. It is a clean test: a simple, verifiable fact about a physical place. It also means most AEO advice for local businesses rests on very little local evidence.

## How we did this research

We re-analyzed the raw records released with Measuring Google AI Overviews: Activation, Source Quality, Claim Fidelity, and Publisher Impact (Xu, Iqbal and Montgomery, IMC 2026). The dataset covers 55,393 trending Google searches in the United States from March 13 to April 21, 2026, including 7,583 AI Overviews, every cited link, the page-one results shown beside each answer, the saved text of cited pages, and fact-check verdicts for 98,020 claims.

* **Local filter.** We tagged searches about a physical business’s hours, open status, closures or “near me,” then read every match by hand. That produced 271 local searches, 207 AI answers and 189 unique questions.
* **Comparison group.** The other 7,376 AI answers in the dataset.
* **Source groups.** Every cited domain was sorted into owner groups, including Gannett newspapers (31 domains) and TEGNA TV stations (13 domains), using their published lists of owned outlets.
* **Replication check.** Our extraction found the same 7,583 AI Overviews the paper reports, and our overall unsupported-claim rate (11.03%) matches its published 11.0%.

**Figure 2. Local “is it open” searches spiked the day after Easter.** 185 of 271 local searches in the dataset were collected on April 6, 2026, the day after Easter, which is why most local answers in this study are about holiday hours. ## How often does Google’s AI answer local business questions?

More often than any other topic: 76.4% of local business searches showed a Google AI Overview, against 13.7% of all searches.

| Climate | 128 | 1735 | 7.4% |
| Beauty & fashion | 5 | 142 | 3.5% |

Embed this figure<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.png" alt="Bar chart of AI Overview activation by category: local business 76.4%, science 39.9%, all others lower" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

**Figure 4. Local searches got an AI answer 76% of the time, even more often than other questions.** Controlling for phrasing, local searches were still 12 points more likely to get an AI Overview than other question-style searches (76.4% vs 64.1%). [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.png)

Data behind this chart

| Group | AI Overview shown | Searches | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local business searches | 207 | 271 | 76.4% |
| Other question-style searches | 2445 | 3812 | 64.1% |
| All searches | 7583 | 55393 | 13.7% |

Embed this figure<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.png" alt="Bar chart: local searches 76.4%, other question searches 64.1%, all searches 13.7% showed an AI Overview" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

Part of the gap is phrasing, because local searches are usually questions and questions trigger AI answers more often. Even against other question-style searches (64.1%), local searches were 12 points more likely to get an AI answer. When someone asks about a place, Google’s AI is the first thing they read.

AEO takeaway

For local questions, the AI answer is now the front door.

### What to do

Find out what AI says about your business today, for the questions customers actually ask: hours, services, prices and “best near me.”

### How Local AI Registry does it

Every business gets a public record on Local AI Registry showing what AI currently says about it, and owners can run a free AI visibility audit to see where answers are wrong or missing.

## Where does Google’s AI get its facts about local businesses?

From the news, not the business. News outlets supplied 67.5% of citations in local answers; businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5%.

**Illustration 2. How Google’s AI builds an answer about a local business.** For local questions, Google’s AI assembled answers mostly from news coverage (67.5% of citations), rarely from the business itself (6.5%), and usually ended by telling people to check with their local store. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.png)

USA Today and its network of local papers (IndyStar, Delaware Online, North Jersey, El Paso Times and dozens more) publish “what’s open” roundups every holiday, and TEGNA’s local TV stations do the same. Google’s AI treats those roundups as the record. Directories barely register: Yelp, MapQuest and OpenTable together supplied 8 of 1,497 local citations.

The vaguer the question, the less the business is cited. For “what’s open today” questions, which is how people discover new places, businesses’ own sites supplied 1.0% of citations. For an independent business that no newspaper writes about, there is no roundup to cite.

AEO takeaway

AI trusts what others publish about you more than what you publish yourself.

### What to do

Get your facts into third-party sources AI already reads: local news, press releases and community roundups. Earned coverage is the citation layer for local answers.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Press releases and media distribution put a business’s confirmed facts on news sites, and the Local AI Registry record itself is an independent third-party source AI can cite.

## Does ranking on Google mean AI will use your website?

No. Brand websites ranked on page one in 147 of 157 brand questions, but the AI cited them in only 70.

**Illustration 3. Ranked first, still skipped: why SEO alone isn’t AEO.** In 147 of 157 brand questions the store’s own site ranked on page one, but the AI cited it in only 70. Ranking and being used by AI are separate outcomes. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.png)

A business site has to rank to be used. AEO takeaway

SEO gets you ranked. AEO gets you used.

### What to do

Write pages that answer one question each in plain sentences, such as “Are you open on Easter?” or “What do you charge for Botox?” Put the answer in the first line, then the details.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s AEO content work builds question-and-answer pages, topical maps and structured data on the client’s own site, so the page that ranks is also the page AI can quote.

## Why does Google’s AI tell people to “check with your local store”?

Because it answers local questions with national facts. 83.6% of local answers hedged, and only 1 of 207 named an address.

**Figure 14. 173 of 207 local AI answers told people to check with their local store.** 83.6% of local AI answers sent the reader back to the store (“check your local store,” “call ahead,” “hours may vary”), against 2.6% of other answers. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle.png)

Data behind this chart

| Group | Hedged |
| --- | --- |
| Local answers | 83.6% |
| Other answers | 2.6% |

Embed this figure<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle.png" alt="Waffle chart of 207 squares, 173 highlighted for answers that hedged with check locally or call ahead" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

**Figure 15. AI answers local questions with national facts.** 65.7% of local answers spoke about “all locations” or “most stores” (vs 2.3% of other answers), and 83.6% hedged (vs 2.6%). National facts are the AI’s default for local questions. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.png)

Data behind this chart

| Measure | Local answers | Other answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tells you to check locally | 83.6% | 2.6% |
| Answers at chain level | 65.7% | 2.3% |
| Gives address or phone | 0.5% | 0.8% |

Embed this figure<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.png" alt="Grouped bar chart: 83.6% of local answers hedge, 65.7% frame the answer at chain level, 0.5% give an address" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

**Figure 16. 1 of 207 local AI answers named a street address or phone number.** Only 1 of 207 local AI answers gave a street address or phone number. The AI answered about chains, not places. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.png)

| Answers | With address or phone |
| --- | --- |
| 207 | 1 |

Embed this figure<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.png" alt="Waffle chart of 207 squares with a single highlighted square for the one answer that gave an address or phone number" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

The AI knows its answer is not about your location, so it hands the question back to the reader. Whoever publishes location-level facts in a form AI can read gets to answer instead of a hedge.

AEO takeaway

Location-level facts are the gap. Fill it and you replace the hedge.

### What to do

Publish your own hours, holiday hours, address, services and prices for your exact location, in plain text and in LocalBusiness structured data, and keep your Google Business Profile current.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry keeps a sourced, dated record of each business. Local AI Registry manages the Google Business Profile, adds LocalBusiness structured data that links back to the verified record, and keeps holiday hours current.

## Can Google’s AI actually read your website?

Often not. When the AI said “the store locator says,” 51.6% of those claims were not supported by any page it cited.

**Figure 17. When Google’s AI says “the store locator says,” half the time it can’t show it.** 16 of 31 local claims that cited a store locator, app or official site (51.6%) were not supported by any page the AI cited, against 6.7% of other local claims. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate.png)

Data behind this chart

| Claim type | Unsupported | Total | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local claims quoting a store locator, app or official site | 16 | 31 | 51.6% |
| All other local claims | 148 | 2,222 | 6.7% |
| Non-local claims quoting an official source | 49 | 465 | 10.5% |

Embed this figure<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate.png" alt="Bar chart: 51.6% of local claims quoting a store locator or app were unsupported, vs 6.7% of other local claims" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

Examples written by the AI and not found in its sources include “The Aldi store locator indicates Easter Sunday: Closed” and “Target Store Locator lists Easter Sunday as closed.” The pattern suggests the AI gets store-level hours from somewhere it does not cite, likely Google’s own business listing data, and attributes them to a locator page it could not read.

**Illustration 4. What Google’s AI can actually read on a page.** News pages the AI cited had about 500 readable words. Store locator pages were mostly scripts, and the median cited social post had 8 readable words. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.png)

Embed this illustration<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.png" alt="Illustration of three page types: a news article full of readable text, a store locator page made mostly of scripts, and a social post with a photo and a few words" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

**Figure 18. Cited vs readable: what Google’s AI could actually read.** News pages were both cited and readable. Social posts were cited in 48% of local answers but 78% were thin (median 8 words). 11% of businesses’ own pages were thin. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.png)

**Figure 19. Social posts the AI cited had a median of 8 readable words.** The median cited social post had 8 readable words. Store locator pages were also thin: Trader Joe’s store search had 97 words and Cracker Barrel’s Easter page 18. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.png)

AEO takeaway

If AI can’t read it, it can’t cite it, and it may misquote it.

### What to do

Keep key facts in plain HTML text, not inside store-locator scripts, images or social posts. A one-page “hours and holidays” page beats a widget. Post updates on your website as well as on Instagram or Facebook.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s technical AEO work makes sites readable to AI crawlers: text versions of key facts, schema markup, an llms.txt file, and readable descriptions on photos and media.

## Do AI answers about local businesses stay the same?

The verdict does; the sources don’t. Different wording of the same question changed about two-thirds of the cited sources.

**Illustration 5. Different wording, different sources, same answer.** Three ways of asking about Target on Easter returned the same verdict but shared only about a third of their sources. No single publisher owns a local answer. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.png)

Embed this illustration<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.png" alt="Illustration of three phrasings of the same Target question, each citing a different mix of websites, all producing the same closed verdict" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

**Figure 20. Ask the same thing in different words and two-thirds of the sources change.** “Is Target open on Easter” and “Target Easter hours,” asked the same day, shared about 35% of cited sources on average. The verdict stayed the same; the sources rotated. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.png)

Across the 46 chains asked about on Easter, the open-or-closed verdict never contradicted itself; every apparent conflict our tagger flagged turned out, when read by hand, to be phrasing like “Yes, it’s closed.” Local answers were also more faithful to their sources than average (7.3% unsupported claims vs 11.1%). But faithful to sources is not the same as accurate for your location, and the sources rotate.

**Illustration 6. One confirmed record, pushed everywhere AI looks.** Because AI rotates between sources, a business’s facts need to match on its website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. Local AI Registry starts from one owner-confirmed record. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png)

Embed this illustration<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png" alt="Diagram of an owner-confirmed Local AI Registry record feeding the business website, Google Business Profile, directories and press, so AI answers match" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/">The Local Answer Gap</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team (2026).</p>

AEO takeaway

Sources rotate, so your facts have to match everywhere.

### What to do

Make your hours, address, services and prices identical on your website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. When the AI swaps one source for another, the answer should not change.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Directory submissions and listing management keep every source in agreement with the owner-confirmed Local AI Registry record, the single source of truth.

AEO closes that gap from both sides. ## Who provides AEO services for local businesses?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) is an answer engine optimization company built for local businesses. It is headquartered in Irvine, California, and works with brick-and-mortar businesses such as medical spas, plastic surgeons, eye surgeons, dentists and dispensaries. Its local AEO services follow the playbook above:

* **A sourced business record.** A public record of what AI says about the business, with every fact sourced and dated.
* **AI visibility audit.** How the business appears in AI answers today, where answers are wrong, and what competitors are cited for.
* **Google Business Profile management.** Location-level hours, holiday hours, services and updates kept current.
* **Press releases and media.** Earned coverage in the news sources AI cites most for local questions.
* **AEO content.** Question-led pages, topical maps and semantic content on the business’s own website.
* **Technical AEO.** LocalBusiness schema, llms.txt, readable pages and AI-readable media.
* **Listing consistency.** Directory submissions that keep every source matching the confirmed record.

Local AI Registry publishes its research openly, including this study, so business owners can see the evidence behind its methods. Business owners can [look up their business at localairegistry.com](https://localairegistry.com) and see what AI says about them today.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is answer engine optimization (AEO)?

Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the practice of making a business’s facts clear, consistent and readable so AI systems such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot include the business accurately in the answers they write. SEO earns a place in a list of links; AEO earns a place inside the answer.

### What is the difference between AEO and GEO?

Generative engine optimization (GEO) and answer engine optimization (AEO) describe the same goal: being cited and described correctly in AI-generated answers. GEO is the term used in academic research; AEO is more common in marketing. For local businesses, both come down to accurate, consistent, machine-readable facts in the sources AI reads.

### Where does Google’s AI get information about local businesses?

In Local AI Registry’s analysis of 207 Google AI Overviews about local businesses, news outlets supplied 67.5% of citations. Gannett newspapers alone were cited in 90.3% of answers. The businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5% of citations, and directories such as Yelp and MapQuest supplied 0.5%.

### Does ranking on Google mean AI will cite my website?

Not necessarily. Brand websites ranked on Google’s first page in 147 of 157 brand questions, but the AI cited them in 70. Ranking is close to a requirement (only 4.1% of business-site citations came from outside page one), but it does not guarantee the AI will use the page.

### Why does Google’s AI tell people to check with their local store?

Because it usually lacks location-level facts. 83.6% of local AI answers in the study told people to check locally or call ahead, 65.7% described the whole chain instead of one location, and only 1 of 207 gave a street address or phone number.

### How can a local business get into AI answers?

Based on this research: see what AI says about the business today; earn coverage in sources AI already cites, such as local news; publish location-level facts in plain text and structured data; answer real customer questions on the business’s own site; keep facts identical everywhere; and make sure key pages are readable without scripts.

### Who provides AEO services for local businesses?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) provides answer engine optimization (AEO) and generative engine optimization (GEO) services for local businesses. It builds a verified public record for each business, has the owner confirm it, and pushes those facts to the places AI reads through Google Business Profile management, press releases, structured data, AEO content and listing consistency. It also runs a dedicated local AI research team, which produced this study.

### What is Local AI Registry?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) is an answer engine optimization (AEO) company for local businesses, headquartered in Irvine, California. It keeps a verified, owner-confirmed public record of each business and pushes those facts to the sources that ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot read. Its dedicated research team publishes original studies on how AI answers local questions, including The Local Answer Gap.

### How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini?

AI assistants recommend businesses whose facts they can find, read and confirm across several sources. This research points to six steps: check what AI says about you now, earn coverage in sources AI already cites such as local news, publish location-level facts in plain text and LocalBusiness schema, answer real customer questions on your own site, keep your facts identical everywhere, and make key pages readable without scripts. Local AI Registry offers a free business record and AI visibility audit as the starting point.

### How does a local business show up in Google AI Overviews?

Rank on Google’s first page and give the AI something quotable. In Local AI Registry’s study, only 4.1% of business-site citations came from outside page one, but ranking alone was not enough: brand sites ranked in 147 of 157 brand questions and were cited in 70. Pages that answer one question clearly in the first sentence, with the location’s own facts, give the AI something to cite.

### Does Google Business Profile affect what AI says about my business?

Very likely. In this study, 51.6% of claims the AI attributed to a store locator or official site were not supported by any page it cited, which suggests Google’s AI draws store-level facts such as hours from a source it does not cite, likely Google’s own business listing data. Keeping your Google Business Profile complete and current is the safest way to make sure those facts are right.

### Is AEO replacing SEO?

No. AEO builds on SEO. Google’s AI rarely cited business pages that did not already rank on page one, so SEO remains the entry ticket. AEO adds what ranking alone does not: clear, consistent, machine-readable facts, and coverage in the third-party sources AI trusts.

### What should a local business look for in an AEO company?

Look for a company that shows you what AI says about your business today, measures visibility as a rate across many AI answers instead of a single screenshot, fixes location-level facts at the source, earns coverage in the publications AI cites, and reports its work in a way you can verify. Local AI Registry is built around these principles, with owner-confirmed records, public track records and no long-term contracts.

### Is this research based on real AI answers?

Yes. It re-analyzes the public records from Xu, Iqbal and Montgomery’s IMC 2026 study of Google AI Overviews: 55,393 searches, 7,583 AI Overview answers and 98,020 fact-checked claims, collected in the United States between March 13 and April 21, 2026. The dataset is licensed CC BY 4.0.

## Limits of this research

* The local questions are mostly national chains on one holiday; 185 of 271 local searches were collected on April 6, 2026, the day after Easter. Independent businesses are not in the data.
* One engine: Google AI Overviews. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot and Google AI Mode may behave differently.
* Claim verdicts come from the original study’s AI judge (Grok 4.1), which its authors audited. We reused their verdicts and did not re-judge.
* Source groups, the local filter and the control levels in the priority map are Local AI Registry’s own rules and judgment. Some counts are small (31 first-party claims, 18 repeat-query pairs), so read those as signals, not settled rates.
* The playbook applies chain-level findings to independent businesses. That is our reasoning from the data, not something the data measured directly.

It is led by a former Google Search executive, advised by a Stanford-trained dermatologist and a Northwestern professor who is a past president of the American Society for Laser Medicine and Surgery, and spread across California, Washington, Texas, New York, Florida, Brazil, Nigeria, Poland, India and Singapore. The team works from raw public data, owns and runs a local med spa, and studies how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot find and describe local businesses.

The team is a dedicated follower of the researchers who built modern AI and those who study AI search, including Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, Yann LeCun, Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Demis Hassabis, Jeff Dean, Ilya Sutskever, Andrej Karpathy, Dario Amodei, Jared Kaplan, Chris Olah, Fei-Fei Li, Andrew Ng, Percy Liang, Karthik Narasimhan, Ameet Deshpande, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Aounon Kumar, Nelson F. Liu, Umar Iqbal and Jacob M. Montgomery. Their work underpins ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, and the team studies their papers and tests their ideas against what AI says about local businesses. No affiliation or endorsement implied. See the [references](#references).

One last thing

AI is evolving every day. So is our playbook.

The engines change how they find, read and cite local businesses constantly, and what worked last quarter may not work next quarter. At Local AI Registry, our dedicated local AI research team keeps testing what works, so the businesses we serve always get the current best approach.

# Sephora Searches Predict Jeuveau Sales

URL: https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/
Updated: 2026-11-18

> Sephora search growth tracks Jeuveau sales at 0.71. Local AI Registry research on 94 searches, med spa clients, Pilates and a Q4 2026 sales estimate.

[Local AI Registry](https://localairegistry.com)  [Research](https://localairegistry.com/research/index.html)  Med Spa Search Signals

Local AI Registry research · Published November 15, 2026

# Med Spa Search Signals: what Google searches reveal about aesthetic clients and sales

By the [Local AI Registry Research Team](#authors)

The short answer

Local AI Registry’s analysis of five years of Google searches shows that a big brand with the same shopper can read a small brand’s sales early. Growth in Sephora searches tracked growth in Jeuveau maker Evolus’s revenue at 0.71 over 15 quarters, while Jeuveau’s own searches scored −0.08. Using Sephora, we estimate Evolus’s Q4 2026 revenue at about $107 million, above the $95 million to $102 million implied by guidance. The same data shows med spa clients live on the Pilates map, men search for surgery but not upkeep, and January to March is research season.

* **94** searches tested as stand-ins
* **15** quarters of company sales
* **49** states compared
* **680** search pairs tested
* **41** charts, maps, explainers and 3D visuals

## Key findings

1. Local AI Registry found that growth in U.S. Google searches for Sephora tracked growth in Evolus revenue (the maker of Jeuveau) at 0.71 across 15 quarters, while searches for Jeuveau itself scored −0.08.
2. Sephora averages about 6.1 million U.S. Google searches a month and Jeuveau about 18,100, so Sephora’s search trend is 338 times larger to read, Local AI Registry found.
3. Using last quarter’s growth plus Sephora searches, Local AI Registry’s estimate landed within 7% of Evolus revenue in 11 of 14 quarters and puts Q4 2026 revenue at about $107M, above the $95M to $102M implied by company guidance.
4. Equinox searches moved opposite to Jeuveau sales over five years (−0.78) but showed no link quarter to quarter (0.02), so a long-trend match alone can mislead, according to Local AI Registry.
5. In 2025, searches for “botox” rose 10% to 16% year over year while Botox Cosmetic sales fell 5% to 12%, which shows “botox” works as a category word, Local AI Registry found.
6. Club Pilates brand searches fell 17% year over year in Q3 2026 while Pilates searches were still up 17% in Q2 2026, and Xponential reported same-store sales down 7.5%, according to Local AI Registry.
7. Across 49 states, Local AI Registry found that searches for med spa treatments follow the same state ranking as Pilates (0.81), Tesla and Rolex (0.75), and run opposite to crockpots and fishing licenses (−0.66).
8. Men make up about 46% of searches for liposuction, facelifts and nose jobs but 22% to 33% of searches for Botox, nails, lashes and spray tans, Local AI Registry found.
9. Local AI Registry found that Botox searches hold near their yearly average in January to March (102) while Botox sales to clinics run 8% below it (92).
10. Of 680 pairs of beauty and everyday searches, only 2 matched on timing, states and age mix, and only 1 of 14 viral “search twin” pairs held up, according to Local AI Registry.

## What is a search signal, and why borrow one from a bigger brand?

A search signal is a trend in how often people search for something on Google. When searches for a product rise, sales often follow. The problem is that many brands are searched too rarely to read. Jeuveau, the wrinkle-relaxing injection made by Evolus, averages about 18,100 U.S. searches a month. Sephora averages about 6.1 million.

So we borrowed the signal. We looked for a much bigger search that shares Jeuveau’s customer and moves with Evolus’s sales. Then we used it to estimate a quarter Evolus has not reported yet. Along the way, we used the same data to describe who the med spa client is, where they live, when they research and what else they buy.

**Illustration 1. Borrow the search signal of a bigger brand with the same shopper.** A niche brand's searches bounce too much to read. A big brand with the same shopper gives a steadier signal to estimate from. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/borrow-a-bigger-search-signal-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/borrow-a-bigger-search-signal-illustration.png)

Embed this illustration<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals#borrow-a-bigger-search-signal-illustration"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/borrow-a-bigger-search-signal-illustration.png" alt="Two panels: Jeuveau with 18,100 monthly searches and a noisy bar pattern; Sephora with 6.1 million searches and a steady rising pattern, arrow pointing to an estimate of Jeuveau sales" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals">Med Spa Search Signals</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team.</p>

**Explainer 1. Why more searches give a steadier signal.** Flip a coin ten times and you might get seven heads. Flip it thousands of times and you get very close to half. Search data behaves the same way, which is why a brand with millions of searches is easier to read than one with thousands. [Animated SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/why-more-searches-are-steadier-explainer.svg)

**Figure 1. Sephora gets 338 times more Google searches than Jeuveau.** Jeuveau averages about 18,100 U.S. searches a month. Sephora averages 6.1 million, so its search trend is far steadier to read. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/monthly-google-searches-sephora-vs-jeuveau.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/monthly-google-searches-sephora-vs-jeuveau.png)

Data behind this chart

| Search | Average monthly U.S. searches |
| --- | --- |
| Sephora | 6120000 |
| Equinox | 368000 |
| Botox | 165000 |
| Jeuveau | 18100 |

Embed this figure<a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals#monthly-google-searches-sephora-vs-jeuveau"><img src="https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/monthly-google-searches-sephora-vs-jeuveau.png" alt="Bar chart of average monthly U.S. Google searches: Sephora 6,120,000, Equinox 368,000, Botox 165,000, Jeuveau 18,100" width="800"></a><p>Source: <a href="https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals">Med Spa Search Signals</a>, Local AI Registry Research Team.</p>

### Terms used in this study

Search signal
:   A trend in how often people search for something on Google, used as an early read on what they will buy.

Proxy search
:   A search for a bigger brand or topic with the same customers, used when the brand you care about gets too few searches to read.

Nowcast
:   An estimate of a period that has already started but has not been reported yet, such as a quarter's sales before the earnings release.

Year-over-year growth
:   The change against the same period a year earlier, which removes normal seasonal ups and downs.

Correlation
:   A number from −1 to 1 that shows how closely two series move together. It shows a match, not a cause.

Category word
:   A word people use for a whole type of product, the way “botox” is used for any wrinkle-relaxing injection.

Search twin
:   Two unrelated searches whose charts move together. We test them on timing, states and age mix to see if the same people are behind them.

Answer engine optimization (AEO)
:   Making a business’s facts clear, consistent and machine-readable so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews include it accurately.

## Has anyone used other brands' searches to estimate aesthetics sales?

Using Google searches to read the economy early is an established idea. Hal Varian and Hyunyoung Choi showed in 2012 that Google Trends data improves near-term estimates of retail sales, car sales and travel. Sharad Goel and colleagues showed in 2010 that searches anticipate box office, game and music sales.

Those studies use searches for the product itself. We could not find published work that estimates aesthetic injectable sales from another brand’s searches, or that tests the med spa client against everyday searches on timing, states and age at once. That is the gap this study fills.

## How we did this research

* Search data: weekly U.S. Google Trends interest for 101 searches from November 2021 to November 2026, each pulled on its own scale, via DataForSEO. 94 had five full years of usable data and were tested as stand-ins.
* Search volume: average monthly U.S. Google searches from Google Ads, November 2025 to October 2026, via DataForSEO.
* Sales: Evolus total net revenue for each quarter from Q1 2022 to Q3 2026 and its 2026 guidance of $330 million to $337 million; AbbVie global Botox Cosmetic net revenue from Q1 2023 to Q3 2026 (Q4 2023 and Q4 2024 are the full year minus the first three quarters); Xponential Fitness results for Q3 2025 to Q3 2026.
* Stand-in test: for each search, we compared growth against the same quarter a year before with Evolus’s revenue growth (15 quarters), then compared the quarter-to-quarter changes in those growth rates. A useful stand-in has to pass both.
* Estimate: Evolus revenue growth predicted from last quarter’s growth and Sephora search growth, tested by hiding one quarter at a time. The Q4 2026 estimate uses Sephora searches from October 4 to November 14, 2026, against the same weeks of 2025.
* States: Google Trends state interest over the past five years for 49 states (Wyoming and Washington, D.C. left out because of small samples). The med spa score averages eight treatment searches after putting each on the same scale. Matches are rank correlations.
* People: DataForSEO’s search panel age and gender mix for 59 searches over the past 12 months, and BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2024 personal care spending by age.
* Search twins: 17 beauty searches against 40 everyday searches (680 pairs), tested on timing (monthly match of 0.50 or more, with and without long trends), states (rank match of 0.35 or more) and age mix (85% overlap or more).
* All aggregated tables are in the [CSV download](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/data/med-spa-search-signals-data.csv).

**Explainer 2. Why we compare with the same time last year.** Most businesses have busy and slow seasons. Comparing January with December makes any business look like it is shrinking. Comparing January with last January removes the season and shows real change. [Animated SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/why-compare-same-time-last-year-explainer.svg)

## Can Sephora searches predict Jeuveau sales?

Yes, better than Jeuveau’s own searches. Sephora search growth matched Evolus revenue growth at 0.71 over 15 quarters; Jeuveau searches scored −0.08.

**Figure 2. Sephora search growth tracks Jeuveau sales growth at 0.71.** Across 15 quarters, Sephora search growth and Evolus revenue growth line up at 0.71. Both slowed through 2024 and both rose in Q2 2026.
